title: Axiomatizations of the proportional division value
headline: Open finding: the sufficiency direction of Theorem 1 fails under its displayed, game-by-game coefficient conditions.

work.title: Axiomatizations of the proportional division value

claims.label: Theorem 1 sufficiency direction
claims.gist: The printed pointwise coefficient restrictions are stated to imply efficiency, weak linearity, and proportional-balanced treatment.
claims.statement: For every individually positive or individually negative TU-game, the displayed representation with coefficients satisfying the displayed same-size restriction implies efficiency, weak linearity, and proportional-balanced treatment.
conditions: The domain consists of TU-games whose singleton worths are all strictly positive or all strictly negative.
The representation and coefficient restriction are imposed separately for each game; the statement does not require coefficients to agree across games.
claims.quantifiers: The theorem compares all games in the stated domain. Weak linearity also compares different games with proportional singleton-worth vectors, while the printed coefficient condition links coefficients only within one game.

result.summary: A value defined on the full three-player domain satisfies the printed representation and coefficient restriction, efficiency, and proportional-balanced treatment, but violates weak linearity at a game and its double.
result.witness: Let N={1,2,3}. For every game with singleton worths x_i of one strict sign, set λ_{ij}=(x_i+x_j)x_k for {i,j,k}=N. Then λ_{ij}/((x_i+x_j)x_k)=1 for each pair, so the same-size restriction holds for every game. For the game v with singleton worths (1,1,1), pair worths (1,2,4), and grand-coalition worth 1, direct substitution gives ψ(v)=(-14/3,4/3,13/3), while ψ(2v)=(-118/3,26/3,98/3).
result.argument: The coefficients are defined for every individually positive or negative singleton vector, and all denominators are nonzero. The representation is efficient and satisfies proportional-balanced treatment by the displayed algebra. The numerical witness has 2ψ(v)=(-28/3,8/3,26/3), which differs from ψ(2v); weak linearity therefore fails even though every nonempty coalition worth in v is positive. The failure is that the pointwise condition permits raw coefficients to change across games with proportional singleton worths.
not_claimed: The necessity direction of Theorem 1 is false.
The intended characterization with an added cross-game coefficient-coherence condition is false.
The proportional division value or later results in the paper are thereby invalidated.
A journal correction has been published.
result.repair_note: A natural candidate repair is to require the raw coefficients to be invariant across games whose singleton-worth vectors lie on the same nonzero line. This note does not establish that a corrected theorem follows in full.

vor_check.detail: The Version of Record PDF was checked at printed page 40 for Theorem 1 and its displayed coefficient conditions.

evidence.detail: A fresh separate-session hostile review checked the theorem reading, full-domain construction, displayed coefficient restriction, three axioms, scaling failure, alternative interpretations, and proposed repair.

author_response.covers: The author agrees with the identified sufficiency gap and counterexample.

history.label: A deep audit identified an open sufficiency-direction finding.
The authors were contacted with the As Stated technical note.

One author agreed with the identified gap and supplied a proposed corrected characterization. A subsequent independent AI review found the proposed correction valid. No official journal corrigendum has yet been published.
The case was released as an Open finding with its As Stated technical note.
